trust_decision.summary: The converter trusts the rank declared in the model proto and indexes Gemm operand shape vectors at fixed positions; the decision to accept or reject an undersized A or B is made in the two Gemm opset adapters, which had no rank guard.

landing_point.why: The report names 'the Gemm version converter adapter' and an undersized input shape; the downward (7->6) adapter is the first place B_shape is read by fixed index, and it is one directory listing away from its upward twin.

version-converter op adapter (header-only, registered at convert.h:236)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route exists to dismiss: the only rank-indexing Gemm code in the tree is the two adapters the fix patches, and the inliner entry point (onnx/inliner/inliner.cc:461) reaches the same adapters through ConvertVersion rather than a second copy. The only live scope trap is placing the fix one layer up (onnx/version_converter.py:17 or convert.cc:16), which the report's own repro would still pass.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: C is a unidirectional-broadcast operand, so rank-1 or scalar C must keep converting; an over-broad fix that demands rank 2 from all three inputs breaks legitimate Gemm conversions (the fix's own tests keep C at shape (4,)).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Gemm opset-1 shape-inference function that reads A/B dims at fixed indices without a rank guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Gemm-1 is the only Gemm schema with no inference function at all (old.cc:2983-3007); a maintainer adding one would mirror the opset-6 body at old.cc:3033-3049 and could easily drop the rank check, and no adapter calls that layer.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-op adapter that rebuilds a rank-2 (M,N) from two operand shape vectors the way the Gemm adapters do
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already compares two operand shape vectors for broadcast and is registered per operator (convert.h:242-247), so a variant that also indexes dims is a natural edit rather than a new concept.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a real Gemm_5_6 adapter replacing the CompatibleAdapter for 5->6 that computes M,N like Gemm_6_7 does
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: 5->6 and 6->5 are the only Gemm hops with no explicit adapter; a maintainer adding per-version Gemm handling would copy the Gemm_6_7 body, which is exactly the shape of code that needs the rank guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Sum 8->7 adapter that indexes operand dims instead of delegating to assert_numpy_multibroadcastable
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Sum already performs the same two-operand broadcast reasoning on the same shape vectors, so an inlined reimplementation with fixed indexes is plausible.

O9_family: heap out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) from an unvalidated tensor rank in the opset version converter

O10_build.toolchain: CMake >= 3.5 era project with protobuf and nanobind; python build via a custom setuptools backend (pyproject requires setuptools>=77, protobuf>=4.25.1)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the reported operand B in gemm_7_6.h (the reproduced 7->6 direction), and/or hoist the rank check into onnx/version_converter.py:17 or convert.cc:16, leaving gemm_6_7.h and the inliner route open.

unverified: repo_mb could not be measured without a shell; ONNX is a large multi-language repository, so tiny_repo/giant_repo were left off rather than guessed.

Whether hidden behavioural tests are expected to enter through onnx.inliner.inline_local_functions(convert_version=True) (onnx/inliner/inliner.cc:461) was not checked against any test fixture; that path needs shape_inference at inliner.cc:419 to supply a declared rank-1 input for a function-local Gemm.
The judgement that onnx/version_converter/helper.cc:79 (assertInputsAvailable's has_sizes/parameter checks) counts as a present-but-ineffective defence at the sink is mine, not a project statement.

The claim that no other rank-indexing Gemm code exists is based on grepping onnx/version_converter for fixed-index shape reads and reading every Gemm schema's inference function; generated/derived code was not exhaustively reviewed.
